issue.title: llm.permission_mode reaches only the coder and reviewer; ~12 other sessions stay on the disabled mode
issue.body:
Follow-up to #220. The `llm.permission_mode` key is resolved inside
`agent/backend.py::make_backend`, so it reaches exactly the two sessions built
through that factory — the coder (`core/runtime.py`) and the reviewer
(`review/reviewer.py`). Every other session constructs `ClaudeBackend`
directly and keeps the class default `bypassPermissions`, which is the mode a
policy-bound organisation disables.

On such an install the task loop is restored and these are not.

## The sites

`grep -rn "ClaudeBackend(" --include='*.py' src/` — the ones that matter are the
sessions that WRITE, because a read-only session degrades quietly while a
writing one fails outright:

* `cli/commands.py:3309` — `nh wiki`. No `readonly=`, so it writes files:
  ```python
  backend = ClaudeBackend(
      model=config.primary_model,
      forbidden_paths=config["safety"]["forbidden_paths"],
  )
  gen = WikiGenerator(backend, max_turns=12)
  ```
* `api/app.py:5990` — the wiki job behind the API, same shape.
* `cli/commands.py:7319 / 7652 / 8596` — the eval, northstar and shadow
  harnesses, all writing.
* `eval/funnel_eval.py:146` — builds `ClaudeBackend` directly and documents
  `permission_mode` as "deliberately NOT passed". That comment is still true;
  it simply predates the key.

Read-only sessions on the same footing: the planner and aggregator
(`core/orchestrator.py`), the intake evaluator, the grill sessions, the
advisory seam, and `nh doctor`'s probe (`agent/backend_check.py:251`).

## The sharper one: the researcher subagent

Every coder attempt is handed a subagent that hardcodes the mode and holds Bash
(`core/orchestrator.py:2448`, wired at `:5771`, pinned by
`tests/test_e2e_orchestrator.py:6074`):

```python
tools=["Read", "Grep", "Glob", "Bash"],
disallowedTools=["Write", "Edit", "MultiEdit", "NotebookEdit"],
permissionMode="bypassPermissions",
```

So after setting the key, the coder runs `acceptEdits` and its own subagent
still asks for the disabled mode. Because the researcher is advisory, watching
one attempt reach a commit does **not** surface this — the attempt succeeds and
the subagent silently returns nothing useful.

## Two related gaps

* **No validation at load.** `load_config` rejects an API key in config, invalid
  role backends and enabled decomposition, but does not check
  `permission_mode`. The value is validated at first backend construction, so a
  misspelling is discovered by a burned attempt rather than at `nh doctor`
  time — for a key whose whole justification is that a silent fallback
  reproduces the symptom, the check belongs at load.
* **`nh doctor` is blind to it.** Its probe constructs `ClaudeBackend` directly
  (`agent/backend_check.py:247-251`), so it cannot report that the configured
  mode is the one the organisation refuses.

## Suggested direction

Route the remaining sessions through `make_backend` (or give `ClaudeBackend` a
config-aware constructor) rather than widening the key's reach site by site.
Until then, `docs/configuration.md` states the coder+reviewer limitation
explicitly, which is the honest interim.

comment.body:
I've just opened PR #308  implementing this! 

The scope is strictly limited to the writing sessions as discussed, and I made sure to preserve the read-only instances for a follow-up. I've also updated the researcher subagent's `permission_mode` to pull from the loaded config, while leaving the `disallowedTools` and the R10 justification completely intact.

Let me know if there's anything else you'd like me to tweak before it merges!

comment.body:
Hi @eyalgolan  — I've gone through the issue and traced the sites in the codebase.

The fix I'm planning:

Route all writing sessions through make_backend — specifically cli/commands.py (wiki, eval, northstar, shadow harnesses) and api/app.py (wiki job), so they pick up llm.permission_mode from config automatically instead of hardcoding the class default.

Fix the researcher subagent at core/orchestrator.py:2448 — the permissionMode="bypassPermissions" is hardcoded there. I'll replace it with a value derived from the loaded config so it respects the operator's setting.

Add validation at load time — check permission_mode inside load_config so a misspelling fails loudly at startup, not mid-attempt after burning tokens.

Fix nh doctor — update agent/backend_check.py:247-251 to route through make_backend so the probe reflects the actual configured mode.

I'll leave read-only sessions (planner, aggregator, intake evaluator, grill, advisory) for a follow-up unless they're in scope here.

Can I be assigned? I'll open a draft PR once I have the core sites done.

issue.title: `getTemplateOrDefault` logs to the console on every call in production — the one unguarded `console.log` in `template-resolver`
issue.body:
`packages/core`'s template resolver guards **every** debug log behind
`process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"` — except the very first one, which runs
unconditionally on every single call.

In the published bundle, `dist/lib/template-resolver.js`:

```js
 9:  console.log(`[getTemplateOrDefault] Called for: ${appPath}`);   // ← no guard
11:    if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development") { ... }
20:      if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development") { ... }
31:    if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development") { ... }
40:      if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development") { ... }
46:  if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development") { ... }
69:  if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development") { ... }
88:      if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development") { ... }
97:        if (process.env.NODE_ENV === "development") { ... }
```

Eight guarded logs and one unguarded, as the first statement of the function. The
surrounding code makes the intent unambiguous: this line was meant to be guarded like its
neighbours.

### Impact

`getTemplateOrDefault` is called during page resolution, so this fires for every template
lookup on every request in production. Two costs:

- **Log noise.** On a hosted platform every line is ingested, stored and billed.
- **Main-thread time.** `console.log` with a template literal is not free, and it runs on
  the serving path.

Neither is catastrophic; both are pure waste, and the fix is a one-line change that matches
what the rest of the file already does.

### Suggested fix

Wrap line 9 in the same `process.env.NODE_ENV === "development"` check used by the other
eight, or drop it — the "Called for" line is the least informative of the set, since the
guarded logs that follow already report the outcome.

---

issue.title: Five more sequence templates
issue.body:
We ship 20. There is room for many more, and this needs no JavaScript at all — just judgement
about outreach.

Wanted, roughly in order of demand:
- **Open-source maintainer to contributor** — someone starred or forked your repo
- **Alumni outreach** — same school or same former employer
- **Customer to case study** — asking a happy customer to go on the record
- **Conference speaker follow-up** — you watched their talk
- **Dormant customer win-back** — churned six months ago

Copy `sequences/warm-connect.json`, change the copy, then:

```bash
node sequences/validate.mjs
```

**Rules the validator enforces:** exactly two variants per invite and message step, 300-character
ceiling, a `|fallback` on every variable, at least 24h between outreach steps, a branch,
`stopOnReply: true`, `autopilot: false`.

**Rules review enforces:** copy a real person would actually send. Nothing from the ban list in
`sequences/README.md`.

**Done when:** the files validate and the table in `sequences/README.md` is updated.
